memory_candidates.content: In a bash script under 'set -euo pipefail', a bare 'python3 << PYEOF ... PYEOF' heredoc invocation followed by 'local exit_code=$?' on the next statement does NOT safely capture the Python process's exit code when it is nonzero -- set -e aborts the script immediately at the heredoc statement itself (it is not part of any conditional context), skipping the capture and any cleanup that follows. Fix: wrap the heredoc in set +e / set -e around the call, and if the result is checked further up an outer loop via a plain statement (fn target; status=$?), convert that to an if/then/else form too -- set -e triggers at every level a bare statement's exit code is inspected after the fact, not just the innermost one.

When excluding non-corpus directories from a recursive find traversal, prefer 'find $target_dir -mindepth 1 ( -name .* -type d -prune ) -o ( -name PATTERN -print )' over a -maxdepth N bound. The -mindepth 1 guard means the prune never tests the traversal's own starting point, so an operator can still explicitly target a dot-named directory (e.g. --dir /path/.backups) and have it indexed, while any dot-prefixed directory found below that starting point -- at any depth, not just the root -- is excluded. A root-only or depth-bounded exclusion misses nested cases (e.g. a stray .chunks/ three levels below a live document's own directory) that a purely at-any-depth predicate catches.
